Let me preface this game with this.
If you are a sim racer, walk away.
If you drift on Asetto Corsa, walk away.
If you take PC driving seriously, walk away.
If you drift in real life and are expecting it to be anything similar, walk away.

This game is not a realistic driver, at all. Cars handle nothing like you would expect them to. But what this game does do well, is fun. It's an amazing arcade drifter. And to be honest, I have more fun playing this than I do play Asetto, because I quite frankly can do what I want and not care, it's a fantastic game to unwind to. Wanna send a car into a wall at 300 km/h and drive away? Go for it. Wanna drift at stupid angles and still drive out of it? Be my guest. This game is an ARCADE DRIFTER, if you are looking for a sim, you have come to the wrong place. This game is absolutely incredible as an arcade drifter. I can't recommend more, me and all my friends have an absolute blast.

- bought the game
- played it for 500 hours
- decided to learn drifting in real life
- bought a car
- learned real life drifting
- crashed it
- back into the game
- played another 350 hours
- bought a new car in real life
- drifted it
- now im happy

After playing it for 2 hours, I decided to write a review for the beginners. Before I bought it I was pretty negative about the fact you had to level up and earn money to buy cars and maps. Within the first 15 minutes, I actually wanted to refund it because the drifting was garbage. After that my dumb ass found out you can put a drifing tune on your car for 8k. So would I recommend this game? YES! After 2 hours you reach level 11 which means you can buy all cars. Making money is also the easiest thing in the world. Personally I play on a wheel and the only thing that is hard is doing tandems. If you play on kbm or controller drifting in this game is easier than learning how to walk. Compared to AC the drifting is a little bit more arcady but that is fine for me. If you' re hesitating to pick this game up, I would say try it and if you don't like it you can always refund it.

In the first few hours you will learn the basics of a good drift. You realize that you can not quickly get into a turn and drift with a crazy speed. Because this is not Need for Speed but it's better than that. After each drift, you will be more proud of yourself because it seems more realistic.

You may need to change your car settings a bit to do a great drift. Although this section is relatively complex, it is worth a try.

The game is beautiful. The number and variety of cars is quite acceptable.

Although I suggest playing this game, there are a few problems:

1- I really want to see a leaderboard for each map. I want to know if I am better than my friends. I want to compete with them for the score of each map and compare my level with them.

2- This game does not provide a simple space for installing maps and car skins through the community. Although there are modes, some of them have bugs and they are not easy to install. Provide something like Left 4 Dead 2 for the community. This game can be legendary if you let the community add infinite maps, skins and cars.

But it seems that the creators have been a little greedy in this area for selling DLCs. This is a big mistake. Three maps and three DLC. I do not want it. I want infinite maps and I want to continue this game forever. So please change the revenue system via DLC and let the real potential of the game be shown.

Absolutely love this game. Whilst I enjoy drifting in other games, I got bored from the lack of maps / good physics / customization / etc, so I decided to buy a new drift game. CarX is pretty fun so far, you have a lot of options for customization, the massive tandems with your friends and people you don't even know are awesome, there's so much more I can say but I'll keep it generally short. I just hope they add more future DLCs soon along with new cars.

I was looking for another racing simulator that replicates real-life driving. I heard feedback suggesting that the game is more arcadish and less realistic, but I decided to give it a shot anyway. While the gameplay was fun and the graphics were amazing, the game didn't meet my expectations as a simulator that applies to real-life driving. Despite enjoying the game and having a great time playing it, I was looking for a more realistic racing simulator. I'll just continue sticking to Assetto Corsa instead.

In summary, if you're looking to learn how to drift realistically, I recommend Assetto Corsa. However, if realism isn't your priority for you, Carx is your game.

[b]CarX Drift Racing Online[/b] offers an enjoyable drifting experience despite its imperfect physics. What sets this game apart is its extensive car customization options, which more than make up for any shortcomings. In other racing games like [i]Forza[/i], players often spend more time customizing their cars than actually racing, and [b]CarX Drift Racing Online[/b] delivers exactly that.

The level of customization in this game is impressive. You have the freedom to create genuine modifications that you would see on real street cars. From painting individual panels to customizing the engine bay, the attention to detail is commendable. It's even possible to remove bumpers and add nudge bars, which adds a unique touch to your vehicle.

Exploring the customization options in [b]CarX Drift Racing Online[/b] feels like stepping into an Autobot repair bay, where you can transform your car into a masterpiece. The ability to personalize your ride to such a detailed extent is a standout feature. It allows players to showcase their creativity and create cars that truly represent their style and preferences.

While the physics may not be flawless, the fun factor of the drifting gameplay helps overlook this aspect. Drifting through corners and maintaining control over your car is a thrilling experience that keeps you engaged. The sense of satisfaction when executing a perfect drift or linking multiple drifts together is unmatched, making you feel like a Decepticon leaving a trail of chaos in your wake.

Despite its focus on customization and drifting, [b]CarX Drift Racing Online[/b] could benefit from further refinement in its physics department. Nevertheless, if you're a fan of car customization and enjoy the adrenaline rush of drifting, this game offers an enjoyable and immersive experience.

Overall, [b]CarX Drift Racing Online[/b] serves as a [u]playground for car enthusiasts[/u] who want to express their creativity through customization. With a wide range of genuine modifications, the game provides endless possibilities to create your dream ride. While the physics may not be flawless, the fun and excitement derived from the drifting gameplay make it a worthwhile experience. Strap in, customize your car, and hit the tracks for some exhilarating drift action.

Time is finally here, and after 360+ hours of playing this game, and interacting with the community and devs on an almost daily basis, its time for my review, going to be honest and in-depth, I hope this may guide you in weather to buy the game or not (spoiler, I dont recommend it, but if you dont mind al these major flaws and just want to play it for a few hours, go for it)

THE GOOD
Let me get this started by saying my first few months playing CarX were great, it started off as a really nice and easy arcade drift game, and having previously played carX on the mobile, was very quickly drawn into buying it

the base its simple, its easy to pick up and there's a fair bit to do as far as cars, customization (wheels, paint, parts, smoke ectect), a decently sized car list, and USE to have a very active modding community making the game stand out even more.
THE BAD
SO, all sounds good and well, BUT the simplicity is very easy to grow board of.

Lack of maps - there's a small selection of maps in carX, for the first week or two it was fun just nailing all the lines and exploring around to see what there is to find, there's not a lot aside from some really, really low poly cars and giant ground planes with no colliders, or just barriers in general blocking logical places to go. 

Ontop of this when you've run Springstone for the 1000032789532578943th F**king time it starts to get really stale, sure you can drift kami but its the same problem again, stale once you run it more than 150 times (that doesn't take a lot of time to do)
Lack of optimization.

This game, in single player runs pretty OKAY I can get stable 60fps running of a GTX670, so if you're on a budget with a shit PC, this game SHOULD be okay for single player, but online is just so poorly done that I will frequently drop from 60 to 30 or less lag spikes when there's more than 8 or so people in a lobby, which again with a dead community, there's usually just one server running with 16+ people, 5 of which are afk, 2 of those people are just trolling / ramming and 3 of the 16 lagging so badly you can barely see their car on the track.

The community is okay if you know people, for the most part lobbies will be chill, there's a lack of trolls (because you can kick people from lobbies, but that doesn't stop them from spam joining over an over again). But for the other part you're getting rammed into a lot of the time even tho you're running a clean, and you bet once they run into you, you will be flamed and voted for a kick.
The devs
I'm sure they all mean well, and it pains me to say this because they probably work pretty hard and want to see this game go far, but it doesn't feel like that, sure theres an obvious language barrier between the English speaking community and the russian devs, but after speaking to some Russians about it even they don't get much information, if any at all for them.

Every question or suggestion for the last year has LITERALLY been the same, "Yes we either know about this problem / think this suggestion would benefit the game, but can't give a time frame or even confirm or deny if its going to be in game"

The last several update (probably since the start of this year) have been random stock cars some good and requested, some terrible and never spoken of, some new kits usually just some over the top rice or just has options to remove body panels that look awful.

Theres never a focus on anything it seems, they just jump from making random verses modes and ignoring the fact the game runs terrible in a populated lobby, the multiplayer desync, all tho has improved a tiny amount, completely ruins any fluidity of online tandems, and whole list of other annoying and or game breaking issues, they rather put more work into verses modes and porting over mobile DLC and selling it to us.

Anyway this turned into more of a rant, but you can ask around the near dead community, a lot of people will agree with me
Smoke a bowl, join a random lobby with "chill" in the title, drift around, live in the moment, love this game.

The game depicts drift almost lifelike. The car can be completely customized in the car, everything can be modified according to my own taste.

[b]If you're looking for a chill, arcade-style racing game, keep scrolling. This is not that. CarX Drift Racing Online is a full-blown addiction, a physics simulator designed to make you feel like a terrible driver for approximately 10 hours before you finally nail that first big corner. It doesn't hold your hand; it slaps your hand away when you try to tap the brakes. The core appeal here is the physics engine, which is responsive, demanding, and incredibly rewarding once you figure out the dark magic of balancing throttle, steering, and clutch kick to maintain a perfect slide. It’s what keeps you coming back for that one perfect tandem run.

The sheer amount of car customization is phenomenal, both visually and mechanically. You can spend more time in the garage fiddling with suspension stiffness, toe angle, and final drive ratios than you do on the track. If you’re a gearhead, the tuning alone is worth the price of entry. Of course, this means you can also completely ruin your car and turn it into an uncontrollable shopping cart, which is part of the fun. The liveries and body kits let you make your virtual ride look exactly like your imaginary drift missile, which is great because there is absolutely no way I could afford to actually damage a real car this much.

Multiplayer is where the magic happens. You’re not just racing; you’re joining lobbies with total strangers on massive open tracks, gracefully, or not-so-gracefully, trying to slide in tandem without slamming into each other. The community is surprisingly welcoming, focusing more on style and flow than winning an arbitrary race. [h1]CarX Drift Racing Online – Precision Drifting at Its Finest[/h1]

[h2]Overall Rating: ★★★★★[/h2]

[b]CarX Drift Racing Online[/b] stands as one of the best experiences in the drifting sim genre. It strikes an impressive balance between deep physics modeling and arcade-style accessibility, all while maintaining a passionate community.

[hr]

[h2]Drifting Mechanics – ★★★★★[/h2]
This is where the game truly shines. The handling feels precise and deeply responsive. Weight transfer, throttle control, and countersteering all feel exactly how you'd expect from a proper drift sim. Whether you prefer realistic tandem battles or style points, CarX has the depth to satisfy.

[hr]

[h2]Customization – ★★★★☆[/h2]
CarX gives you full control over vehicle performance and appearance. From tire pressure to camber angles, and even vinyl editing for liveries, the customization tools are excellent. The only thing it lacks is a broader range of engine swaps or cosmetic body kits.

[hr]

[h2]Track Selection – ★★★☆☆[/h2]
The variety is good, but after long hours, it can begin to feel repetitive. Fortunately, mod support and community maps add extended replay value.

[hr]

[h2]Multiplayer and Community – ★★★★☆[/h2]
Lobbies are active, and the online experience is generally smooth. There’s a strong scene for tandem drifting, car meets, and competitions. Still, server stability and occasional disruptive players remain minor issues.

[hr]

[h2]Visuals and Audio – ★★★★☆[/h2]
While not pushing the limits graphically, CarX’s visuals are clean and stylish. The tire smoke, lighting, and detail are more than enough to immerse. Engine sounds are decent but a bit repetitive across the car list.

[hr]

[h2]Newcomer Advice[/h2]
[i]For new players:[/i]
– Start with a stable car like the [b]Wanderer L30[/b] or [b]Hachi-Roku[/b].
– Use [b]Comfort tires[/b] until you master throttle control.
– Try [u]Training Mode[/u] or solo free runs to build confidence.
– Avoid going online too early – the skill gap can be punishing.

[hr]

[h2]Final Thoughts[/h2]
[b]CarX Drift Racing Online[/b] is a love letter to drifting. It doesn’t have the budget of AAA racers, but its physics and depth easily rival them. Whether you're aiming for style or precision, this is one of the best sideways driving experiences available today.

CarX Drift Racing Online is a high-octane, adrenaline-fueled masterpiece for fans of competitive drifting. The game strikes an impressive balance between accessibility and depth, offering satisfying gameplay for beginners while providing a steep learning curve for those looking to perfect their skills.

The car physics are a standout feature, delivering a realistic yet approachable driving experience. Whether you’re sliding through tight turns or nailing the perfect tandem drift, the handling feels precise and responsive. The ability to customize cars with detailed tuning and styling options adds a personal touch, letting you create a ride that feels uniquely yours.

Multiplayer is where CarX truly shines. Whether you’re competing in ranked battles, chilling in free ride lobbies, or participating in online competitions, the sense of community elevates the game. With its vibrant user base, there's always someone to challenge or team up with.

While the track selection is solid and offers a variety of terrains, some players might crave more frequent updates to keep things fresh. Additionally, the game’s visuals, while beautiful and polished, can feel slightly dated compared to modern racing titles.
